{{Short description|Edible fruit-bearing species of plant}} {{for|the thoroughbred racehorse|Cherimoya (horse)}} {{Speciesbox | image = Cherimoya tree hg.jpg | image_caption = Branch with leaves and fruit | status = LC | status_system = IUCN3.1 | status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Botanic Gardens Conservation International (BGCI). |author2=IUCN SSC Global Tree Specialist Group. |year=2019 |title=''Annona cherimola'' |volume=2019 |article-number=e.T143324599A143324601 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2019-1.RLTS.T143324599A143324601.en |language=en |access-date=30 March 2026}} | genus = Annona | species = cherimola | authority = [[Philip Miller|Mill.]] | range_map = Range of Annona cherimola-Current.svg | range_map_caption = Current range of native and naturalized ''A. cherimola'' | synonyms = ''Annona pubescens'' Salisb.
''Annona tripetala'' Aiton
''Annona cherimolia'' Mill. [[Orthographical variant|orth. var.]]{{IPNI|id=72172-1|taxon=Annona cherimolia}} | synonyms_ref = {{GRIN | ''Annona cherimola'' | 3479 | accessdate = 2008-04-17}} }} The '''cherimoya''' ('''''Annona cherimola''''') is a species of fruit-bearing plant in the genus ''[[Annona]]'', within the family [[Annonaceae]], which also includes the closely related [[sweetsop]] and [[soursop]]. Native to mountainous regions of [[Honduras]] and [[Guatemala]], the plant has a long history of cultivation in the [[Andes]] and [[Central America]], and is now grown in tropical and subtropical regions around the world. The edible fruit is generally well regarded. ==Description== ''Annona cherimola'' is a fairly dense, fast-growing, woody,{{cite web | url = http://www.worldagroforestrycentre.org/sea/Products/AFDbases/af/asp/SpeciesInfo.asp?SpID=1728 | title = Current name: ''Annona cherimola'' | access-date = 2008-04-17 | work = AgroForestryTree Database | publisher = International Center For Research In Agroforestry | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110930042220/http://www.worldagroforestrycentre.org/sea/products/afdbases/af/asp/SpeciesInfo.asp?SpID=1728 | archive-date = 2011-09-30 }} briefly [[deciduous]]{{cite web | url = http://titanarum.uconn.edu/199500093.html | title = ''Annona cherimola'' Mill. | access-date = 2008-04-17 | author = EEB Greenhouse Staff, University of Connecticut | author-link = University of Connecticut | date = 2008-04-10 | work = Ecology & Evolutionary Biology Greenhouses }} but mostly [[evergreen]], low-branched, spreading tree or shrub. It is {{convert|5 to 9|m|ft|abbr=off}} tall. Mature branches are sappy and woody. Young branches and twigs have a matting of short, fine, rust-colored hairs.{{cite book|author=Wiggins, I. L.|author2=Porter, D. M.|date=1971|title=Flora of the Galapágos Islands|publisher=Stanford University Press|pages=521–522|url=http://www.hear.org/pier/references/pierref000209.htm}} Via {{cite web | url = http://www.hear.org/pier/species/annona_cherimola.htm | title = ''Annona cherimola'' (PIER Species info) | access-date = 2008-04-17 | author = Pacific Island Ecosystems at Risk (PIER) | author-link = Hawaiian Ecosystems at Risk project | date = 2008-04-09 | work = PIER species lists | publisher = [[United States Geological Survey]] & [[United States Forest Service]] | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20070715190852/http://www.hear.org/Pier/species/annona_cherimola.htm| archive-date=July 15, 2007| url-status= live}} The leathery [[leaves]] are {{convert|5–25|cm|frac=2}} long{{cite web | url = http://ntbg.org/herbarium/detail.php?tempid=20352 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110724111613/http://ntbg.org/herbarium/detail.php?tempid=20352 | archive-date = 2011-07-24 | title = Record Detail ANNONACEAE ''Annona cherimola'' Mill. | access-date = 2008-04-17 | last = Flynn | first = Tim | date = 2002-05-22 | work = Herbarium Database | publisher = [[National Tropical Botanical Garden]] }} {{convert|3–10|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} wide, and mostly elliptic, pointed at the ends and rounded near the leaf stalk. When young, they are covered with soft, fine, tangled, rust-colored hairs. When mature, the leaves bear hairs only along the veins on the undersurface. The tops are hairless and a dull medium green with paler veins, the backs are velvety, dull grey-green with raised pale green veins. New leaves are whitish below. The leaves are single and alternate, dark green, and slightly hairy on the top surface. They attach to branches with stout {{convert|6–10|mm|abbr=off|frac=8}} long and densely hairy leaf stalks. Cherimoya trees bear very pale green, fleshy flowers. They are {{convert|3|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} long with a very strong, fruity odor. Each flower has three outer, greenish, fleshy, oblong, downy [[petals]] and three smaller, pinkish inner petals with yellow or brown, finely matted hairs outside, whitish with purple spots and many [[stamen]]s on the inside. Flowers appear on the branches opposite to the leaves, solitary or in pairs or groups of three, on flower stalks that are covered densely with fine rust-colored hairs, {{convert|8|–|12|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}} long. The buds are {{convert|15–18|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}} long and {{convert|5–8|mm|abbr=on|frac=8}} wide at the base. The pollen is shed as permanent tetrads.{{cite journal|vauthors= Lora J, Testillano PS, Risueño MC, Hormaza JI, Herrero M|title=Pollen development in ''Annona cherimola'' Mill. (Annonaceae). Implications for the evolution of aggregated pollen|journal=BMC Plant Biology|volume=9|issue=1|year=2009|article-number=129|issn=1471-2229|doi=10.1186/1471-2229-9-129|pmid=19874617|pmc=2774696|bibcode=2009BMCPB...9..129L |doi-access=free}} ===Fruits=== The edible cherimoya fruit is a large, green, conical or heart-shaped compound fruit, {{convert|10–20|cm|abbr=on|frac=2}} long, with diameters of {{convert|5–10|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}}, and skin that gives the appearance of having overlapping scales or knobby warts. They ripen to brown with a fissured surface in late winter and early spring; they weigh on the average {{convert|150|–|500|g|oz|lk=on|abbr=off}}, but extra-large specimens may weigh {{convert|2.7|kg|lb|abbr=off|sigfig=1}} or more. Cherimoya fruits are commercially classified according to degree of surface irregularity, as follows:{{cite web|author=Morton, JF|year=1987|url=https://www.hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/morton/cherimoya.html|title=Cherimoya, in Fruits of Warm Climates, pp. 65–69|publisher=Center for New Crops and Plant Products, Purdue University Department of Horticulture and Landscape Architecture}} 'Lisa', almost smooth, difficult to discern areoles; 'Impresa', with "fingerprint" depressions; 'Umbonata', with rounded protrusions at the apex of each areole; 'Mamilata' with fleshy, nipple-like protrusions; or 'Tuberculata', with conical protrusions having wart-like tips. The flesh of the cherimoya contains numerous hard, inedible, black, bean-like, glossy seeds, {{convert|1–2|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} long and about half as wide. Cherimoya seeds are poisonous if crushed open. Like other members of the family Annonaceae, the entire plant contains small amounts of neurotoxic [[acetogenin]]s, such as [[annonacin]], which appear to be linked to atypical [[parkinsonism]] in [[Guadeloupe]].{{cite journal|pmid=16078200 | doi=10.1002/mds.20632 | volume=20 | issue=12 | title=Quantification of acetogenins in Annona muricata linked to atypical parkinsonism in guadeloupe |date=December 2005 | journal=[[Mov. Disord.]] | pages=1629–3 |vauthors=Champy P, etal | s2cid=31508365 }} Moreover, an extract of the bark can induce paralysis if injected. {{gallery|mode=packed |Cherimoya fruit hg.jpg|Ripe cherimoya fruits |Cherimoya cut hg.jpg|Split cherimoya fruit |Annona cherimola seeds - (2).jpg|Cherimoya seeds }} == Etymology == The name is derived from the [[Quechua languages|Quechua]] word ''{{lang|qu|chirimuya}}'', which means "cold seeds". The plant grows at high altitudes, where the weather is colder, and the seeds will germinate at higher altitudes. In Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela, the fruit is commonly known as ''chirimoya'' (spelled according to the rules of the Spanish language). It is also spelled '''cherimoyer'''.{{cite web|url=https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/cherimoyer|title=CHERIMOYER definition and meaning|website=Collins English Dictionary|publisher=HarperCollins Publishers|access-date=16 November 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.dictionary.com/browse/cherimoya|title=Cherimoya Definition & Meaning|website=Dictionary.com|publisher=Dictionary.com, LLC|access-date=16 November 2025}} It is also called the '''custard apple{{GRIN | ''Annona cherimola'' | 3479 |access-date=2008-04-21}}''' due to the creamy texture of the fruit's flesh. == Distribution and habitat == [[File:Bosque nativo de chirimoyos ecuatorianos.jpg|thumb|Region of wild cherimoyas in [[Vilcabamba, Ecuador]]]] [[File:Wild cherimoya plant Vilcabamba Ecuador.jpg|thumb|upright|A wild cherimoya plant in Vilcabamba]] Widely cultivated nowadays across tropical and subtropical regions of the world, ''A. cherimola'' originated in upland regions of the Americas. Once believed to be native to the Andes of Ecuador and Peru, genetic research places its origin in [[Honduras]] and [[Guatemala]].{{cite web |last1=N. Larranaga |title=A Mesoamerican origin of cherimoya (Annona cherimola Mill.): Implications for the conservation of plant genetic resources |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/mec.14157?saml_referrer |access-date=13 March 2026}} Here, the genetic diversity was found to be the greatest. From its mesoamerican homeland humans brought the plant to South America about 4,000 years ago.{{cite web |last1=N. Larranaga |title=A Mesoamerican origin of cherimoya (Annona cherimola Mill.): Implications for the conservation of plant genetic resources |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/mec.14157?saml_referrer |access-date=13 March 2026}} Beginning in the 18th century, the cherimoya was distributed across the globe by Europeans. ==Ecology== ===Pollination=== [[File:Cherimoya sprouts emerging.jpg|thumb|upright|Cherimoya sprouts emerging]] [[File:Nitidulidae's beetle visiting cherimoya's flowers.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Sap beetle|Nitidulidae]] beetle on cherimoya flower, [[Jundiaí]], Brazil]] The flowers of ''A. cherimola'' are [[hermaphroditic]] and have a mechanism to avoid self-pollination. The short-lived flowers open as female, then progress to a later, male stage in a matter of hours. This requires a type of pollinator that not only collects the pollen from flowers in the male stage but also deposits it in flowers during the female stage. Because cherimoya's genus, ''[[Annona]]'', includes subtropical species greatly valued for human food and ecosystem services, its pollinators have been well studied. A 2017 publication points to small [[sap beetle|nitidulid sap beetle]]s as the key pollinators:
Beetles arrived at the flowers with their bodies covered in pollen and these pollen grains were transferred to the stigmata while foraging on nutritious tissues at the base of the petals. With dehiscence of the stamens and retention within the floral chamber, the bodies of the floral visitors were again covered with pollen which they carried to newly opened flowers, thus promoting the cycle of pollination.{{cite journal | display-authors=etal | last1=Silva Costa |first1=Marilza |title=Beetle pollination and flowering rhythm of Annona coriacea Mart. (Annonaceae) in Brazilian cerrado: Behavioral features of its principal pollinators |journal=PLOS ONE |date=February 2017 |volume=12 |issue=2 | article-number=e0171092 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0171092 | bibcode=2017PLoSO..1271092C | doi-access=free |pmc=5289549 }}
Because the beetle pollinators are not strong fliers, their entire lifecycle must be facilitated onsite in both orchard and forest restoration settings. The flower itself offers the ideal copulation chamber after beetles enter during the female (earliest) stage. At the inner base of the petals are nutritious tissues called "power bodies" on which the beetles feed until the male stage peaks. Exiting the flower at that time, pollen attaches to the bodies of the beetles, which they carry to yet another flower in its female stage. There, another round of feeding and possible copulation ensues. Abundant leaves, rotting fruit, and other organic material on the ground beneath or near the flowering ''Annona'' species are crucial for the larval stage of the beetle. There eggs are laid, the larvae hatch and feed on decaying matter, then digging downward into the soil layer to pupate. Beetles emerge when flowering begins the following year. In orchards distant from wild habitat, pollination by hand may be necessary. Growers use a small paint brush to collect the pollen from the male stage of flowers and then to also transfer pollen to the female stage. Another method is to encourage the sap beetles to engage in full life cycles, primarily by allowing leaf litter to accumulate and some fallen fruits to remain beneath the trees.{{cite web |last1=Barlow |first1=Connie |title=Pawpaw Ecological Survey in Michigan Part 1: Who Are the Pollinators? |url=https://www.torreyaguardians.org/pawpaw-ecological-michigan-pollinators.html#part-1 |website=torreyaguardians.org |access-date=18 November 2025}} ===Climate requirements=== In the tropics the cherimoya grows at altitudes of {{convert|700 to 2400|m|abbr=on}}, requiring warm-temperate conditions throughout the year, only tolerating occasional light frosts. In Guatemala the tree thrives at elevations of {{convert|1200 to 1800|m|abbr=on}} with {{convert|1300|mm|in|abbr=on}} of rainfall with a pronounced dry season. The evaluation of 20 locations in [[Loja, Ecuador|Loja Province]], Ecuador, indicated certain growing preferences of wild cherimoya, including altitude between {{Convert|1500 and 2000|m|abbr=on}}, optimum annual temperature range between {{Convert|18 and 20|C|F}}, annual precipitation between {{Convert|800 and 1000|mm|abbr=on}}, and soils with high sand content and slightly acidic properties with [[Soil pH|pH]] between 5.0 and 6.5.{{cite web|url=https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/522063/file/1874191|title=Distribution and potential of cherimoya (''Annona cherimoya'' Mill.) and highland papayas (''Vasconcellea'' spp.) in Ecuador|author=Scheldeman, Xavier|date=2002|publisher=University of Ghent }} ==Cultivation== The plant has a long history of cultivation in the Andes and Central America.{{cite journal |vauthors=van Zonneveld M, Scheldeman X, Escribano P, Viruel MA, Van Damme P, Garcia W, Tapia C, Romero J, Sigueñas M, Hormaza JI|year=2012|title=Mapping Genetic Diversity of Cherimoya (''Annona cherimola'' Mill.): Application of Spatial Analysis for Conservation and Use of Plant Genetic Resources|journal=[[PLoS ONE]]|volume=7|issue=1|article-number=e29845|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0029845|doi-access=free|pmid=22253801|pmc=3253804|bibcode=2012PLoSO...729845V}} Today it is grown in tropical and subtropical regions throughout the world, including Central America, northern South America, southern California, South Asia, Australia, the [[Mediterranean region]], and North Africa.{{cite web |title=Cherimoya in Germany |url=https://www.importpromotiondesk.de/fileadmin/user_upload/Publikationen/factsheet/obst_gemuese/cherimoya-in-germany.pdf |publisher=Import Promotion Desk (IPD), [[Center for the Promotion of Imports]] |access-date=22 May 2021 |archive-date=22 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522234209/https://www.importpromotiondesk.de/fileadmin/user_upload/Publikationen/factsheet/obst_gemuese/cherimoya-in-germany.pdf }} In Chile, it has traditionally been cultivated in the valleys and oases of the north, as far south as the [[Aconcagua River|valley of Aconcagua]].{{Cite book |title=Chile: Plantas alimentarias Prehispánicas |last1=Pardo B. |first1=Oriana |publisher=Ediciones Parina |year=2014 |isbn=978-956-9120-02-2 |edition=2015 |location=[[Arica]], Chile |pages=169–170 |language=Spanish |last2=Pizarro |first2=José Luis}} In the Mediterranean region, it is cultivated mainly in southern Spain and [[Madeira]], where it enjoys [[Protected designation of origin|protected designation of origin status]],{{Cite web |date=April 16, 2024 |title=A anona (história) |url=https://www.madeira.gov.pt/drc/pesquisar/ctl/ReadInformcao/mid/7602/InformacaoId/219384/UnidadeOrganicaId/57/LiveSearch/Anona |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Direcção Regional da Cultura}} where it was introduced between 1751 and 1797, after which it was carried to Italy, but now can also be found in several countries of Africa, the Middle East, and [[Oceania]]. It is cultivated throughout the Americas, including Hawaii since 1790 and California, where it was introduced in 1871. In Western horticulture, growers are often advised to grow cherimoya in full sun,{{Cite web|last=Grant|first=Amy|title=What Is A Cherimoya – Cherimoya Tree Info And Care Tips|url=https://www.gardeningknowhow.com/ornamental/trees/annona/cherimoya-tree-info-and-care.htm|website=Gardening Know How|date=4 December 2022 }} while the plant has been considered shade-tolerant in Japan.{{Cite web|last=小林|first=里穂|title=世界三大美果のひとつ【チェリモヤ】は天然のアイスクリームの味？|url=https://www.olive-hitomawashi.com/column/2019/09/post-6444.html|access-date=11 January 2021|website=オリーブオイルをひとまわし}} In 2001, a study conducted by [[Kyoto University]] showed that shading of 50–70% sunlight was adequate to obtain an optimal light environment.{{Cite journal|last=Higuchi|first=Hirokazu|date=19 February 2001|title=Shading Responses of Cherimoya Leaf Chlorophyll Content, Leaf Morphology, Shoot Growth, Leaf Gas Exchange and Fruit Production under Plastic House Conditions|url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/ecb1963/39/4/39_4_255/_pdf|journal=Environment Control in Biology|volume=39|issue=4|pages=255–265|doi=10.2525/ecb1963.39.255|doi-access=free}} {{gallery|mode=packed |Cherimoya_plantage_hg.jpg|Plantation in southern [[Andalucia]] |Annona cherimola fruit, Pedra Bela, Brazil.jpg|Cherimoya fruit cultivated in [[Pedra Bela]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]], [[Brazil]] }} ===Cultivars=== {{main|List of cherimoya cultivars}} The cherimoya of the Granada-Málaga tropical coast in Spain is a fruit of the cultivar 'Fino de Jete' with the [[Protected designation of origin|EU's protected designation of origin appellation]].{{cite web|title=COUNCIL REGULATION (EC) No 510/2006 'CHIRIMOYA DE LA COSTA TROPICAL DE GRANADA-MÁLAGA'|url=http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:C:2009:197:0010:0013:EN:PDF|publisher=EU DOOR|access-date=24 March 2014}} 'Fino de Jete' fruits have skin type Impressa and are smooth or slightly concave at the edges. The fruit is round, oval, heart-shaped, or kidney-shaped. The seeds are enclosed in the carpels and so do not detach easily. The flavor balances intense sweetness with slight acidity and the soluble sugar content exceeds 17° Bx. According to the [[Official Journal of the European Union]], the variety is prepared and packed in the geographical area because:
it is a very delicate, perishable fruit and its skin is very susceptible to browning caused by mechanical damage, such as rubbing, knocks, etc. The fruit must be handled with extreme care, from picking by hand in the field to packing in the warehouse, which must be carried out within 24 hours. Repacking or further handling is strictly forbidden.
[[File:Bin Lang Taiwan Cherimoya-fruits-01.jpg|thumb|upright|A cherimoya fruit, growing in a protective cover on a plantation in Bin Lang Village, Taiwan]] ''Annona cherimola'', preferring the cool Andean altitudes, readily hybridizes with other ''[[Annona]]'' species. A hybrid with ''[[Annona squamosa|A. squamosa]]'' called [[atemoya]] has received some attention in West Africa, Australia, Brazil, and Florida.{{cite web |url=https://plants.jstor.org/stable/10.5555/al.ap.upwta.1_227 |title=Annona cherimola Mill. [family ANNONACEAE] |access-date=2019-09-05 |work=Global Plants |publisher=JSTOR }} ===Harvest=== Large fruits which are uniformly green, without cracks or mostly browned skin, are best. The optimum temperature for storage is {{convert|8|–|12|C|F}}, depending on cultivar, ripeness stage, and duration, with an optimum relative humidity of 90–95%. Unripe cherimoyas will ripen at room temperature, when they will yield to gentle pressure. Exposure to [[Ethylene as a plant hormone|ethylene]] (100 ppm for one to two days) accelerates ripening of mature green cherimoya and other ''Annona'' fruits; they can ripen in about five days if kept at {{convert|15|to|20|C|F}}. Ethylene removal can also be helpful in slowing the ripening of mature green fruits. ==Nutrition and edibility== {{Cookbook|Cherimoya}} Raw cherimoya fruit is 79% water, 18% [[carbohydrate]], 2% [[protein (nutrient)|protein]], and 1% [[fat]]. In a {{cvt|100|g}} reference amount providing 75 [[calorie]]s, cherimoya is a moderate source (10–15% of the [[Daily Value]]) of [[vitamin C]], [[vitamin B6|vitamin B6]], [[riboflavin]], and [[potassium in biology|potassium]], with no other [[micronutrient]]s in significant content. {{nutritional value | name=Cherimoya, raw | image=Chirimoya fruit.jpg | kJ=313 | protein=1.57 g | fat=0.68 g | carbs=17.71 g | fiber=3 g | sugars=12.87 | calcium_mg=10 | iron_mg=0.27 | magnesium_mg=17 | phosphorus_mg=26 | potassium_mg=287 | sodium_mg=7 | zinc_mg=0.16 | manganese_mg=0.093 | vitC_mg=12.6 | thiamin_mg=0.101 | riboflavin_mg=0.131 | niacin_mg=0.644 | pantothenic_mg=0.345 | vitB6_mg=0.257 | folate_ug=23 | vitE_mg=0.27 | water=79.4 g | source_usda = 1 | note=[https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/173953/nutrients Link to USDA Database entry] }} According to botanist [[Berthold Carl Seemann]],
The pineapple, the [[mangosteen]], and the cherimoya are considered the finest fruits in the world, and I have tasted them in those localities where they are supposed to attain their highest perfection – the pineapple in [[Guayaquil]], the mangosteen in the [[East Indian Archipelago|Indian Archipelago]], and the cherimoya on the slopes of the Andes, and if I were asked which would be the best fruit, I would choose without hesitation, cherimoya. Its taste, indeed, surpasses that of every other fruit, and [[Thaddäus Haenke|Haenke]] was quite right when he called it the masterpiece of Nature.{{cite book |last=Popenoe |first=Wilson |year=1945|chapter=The Underdeveloped Field of Tropical Fruits|title=New Crops for the New World|editor1-last=Wilson|editor1-first=C.M.|location=New York|publisher=The MacMillan Co |page=17}}
The fruits require storage at {{convert|50|F}} to inhibit softening and maintain edibility. Different varieties have different flavors, textures, and shapes. The flavor of the flesh ranges from mellow sweet to tangy or acidic sweet, with variable suggestions of pineapple, banana, pear, papaya, strawberry or other berry, and apple, depending on the variety. The ripened flesh is creamy white. When ripe, the skin is green and gives slightly to pressure. Some characterize the fruit flavor as a blend of banana, pineapple, papaya, peach, and strawberry.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bioversityinternational.org/fileadmin/user_upload/online_library/publications/pdfs/1303.pdf|title=Descriptors for cherimoya (Annona cherimola Mill.)|date=2008|website=Bioversity International|publisher=Bioversity International and CHERLA|access-date=19 March 2019}} The fruit can be chilled and eaten with a spoon, which has earned it another nickname, the "ice cream fruit". In Chile and Peru, it is commonly used in ice creams and yogurt.{{cite book| url=http://www.nap.edu/catalog/1398/lost-crops-of-the-incas-little-known-plants-of-the | chapter-url=http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=1398&page=228 |chapter =Cherimoya |title= Lost crops of the Incas: Little-known plants of the Andes with promise for worldwide cultivation | publisher=[[National Academy Press]] | vauthors=Popenoe H, King SR, León J, Kalinowski LS, Vietmeyer ND | veditors=((National Research Council)) | year=1989 | location=Washington, D.C. | pages=228–239 | isbn=978-0-309-07461-2|display-authors=etal|doi = 10.17226/1398}} When the fruit is ripe and still has the fresh, fully mature green-yellow skin color, the texture is like that of a soft ripe pear or papaya. When the skin turns brown at room temperature, the fruit is no longer good for human consumption.{{cn|date=January 2021}} ==Brand== Chirimoya Cumbe is a well-known case involving [[Collective trade mark|collective marks]] in [[trademark law]].{{Cite web |last=lawcirca |date=2020-07-19 |title=Collective Marks under the Trademark Act - Law Circa |work=Law Circa |url=https://lawcirca.com/collective-marks-under-the-trademark-act/ |access-date=2023-04-12 |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Name Matters |url=https://www.wipo.int/ipadvantage/en/details.jsp?id=2561 |access-date=2023-04-12 |website=www.wipo.int |language=en}}{{Creative Commons text attribution notice|cc=by4|from this source=yes}} The [[World Intellectual Property Organization]] has defined these collective marks as "signs which distinguish the geographical origin, material, mode of manufacturing or other common characteristics of goods or services of different enterprises using the collective mark." The owner of a collective mark are members of an association of such enterprises. Cumbe is a valley in the [[Huarochirí Province|Huarochiri province]] of Peru where the climatic conditions are favourable for growing chirimoya. The fruit produced in the Cumbe valley is considered of superior quality, with a large fruit size, soft skin, low seed index (number of seeds per 100 grams of fruit), and high nutrient value. In 1997, Matildo Pérez, a peasant from a village community in the heights of Lima, decided to apply personally to the [[INDECOPI|National Institute for the Defense of Competition and Intellectual Property of Peru]] (INDECOPI) for the registration of the trademark "Chirimoya Cumbe". The application was refused since no exclusive rights in generic names can be granted to a single person. Mr. Pérez appeared at INDECOPI again, this time with a delegation headed by the Deputy Mayor of Cumbe, to register the "Chirimoya Cumbe" as a trademark which would give the community in Lima exclusive rights with respect to the name "Cumbe". The INDECOPI officials explained that "Chirimoya Cumbe" is in fact an [[Geographical indication|appellation of origin]], not a trademark. To be more precise, the word "Cumbe" is an appellation of Peruvian origin, because the valley of Cumbe is a geographical area that gives certain distinctive properties to the Chirimoya grown there. [[File:Chirimoyamuseolarco.jpg|thumb|[[Moche (culture)|Moche]] ceramic cherimoya, 200 BC, [[Larco Museum]] collection in [[Lima]]]] [[File:Cherimoya bottle Cupisnique pre-columbian santiago.JPG|thumb|Cherimoya-shaped bottle made by the [[Cupisnique]] culture {{circa|1000 to 700 BC}}, [[Chala]] region, Peru]] The people of Cumbe declined the proposition of appellation of origin: "It is said that with appellations of origin the State is the owner, and it is the State that authorizes use, and that is why we are saying no. We do not want the State to be the owner of the 'Cumbe' name."{{cn|date=July 2023}} After lengthy search for solutions, it was suggested that "Chirimoya Cumbe" should be registered as a "collective mark", the owners of which would be the people of Cumbe and which would be used according to rules that they themselves would lay down. In 2022, the name "Chirimoya Cumbe" has its own characteristic logo and is registered as a collective mark in the name of the village of Santo Toribio de Cumbe (in Class 31 of the International Classification). ==In culture== The [[Moche (culture)|Moche]] culture of Peru had a fascination with agriculture and represented fruits and vegetables in their art; cherimoyas were often depicted in their ceramics.Berrin, Katherine & [[Larco Museum]]. ''The Spirit of Ancient Peru: Treasures from the Museo Arqueológico Rafael Larco Herrera.'' New York: [[Thames and Hudson]], 1997.
